title: The Exhibition at Université du Luxembourg- From Oct. 13 to 29, 2026
content:
The Source Code Exhibition will be on display from 13 to 29 October 2026 on the ground floor of the Maison du Savoir at the University of Luxembourg.

Join us for the opening event on Tuesday, 13 October, from 16.00 to 18.30. The programme will begin with a round-table discussion held in the auditorium 3330.

The roundtable, moderated by Valérie Schafer, will gather curators of the exhibition, Mathilde Fichen, Titaÿna Kauffmann Will, Stefano Penge and Camille Picard, as well as two contributors, Stéphane Bortzmeyer and Kate Mancey.

Afterwards, we will visit the exhibition with drinks and snacks.

The event is free, but registration is welcome. Register for opening afternoon 

Maison du Savoir

https://www.uni.lu/c2dh-en/events/source-code-exhibition/

title: The Exhibition at SFSCON in Bolzano – From Nov. 13 to Dec. 19 2026
content:
The Source Code Exhibition will be installed during SFSCON, in Bolzano (Italy), from 13-14 November 2026, and on display until 19 December 2026.

SFSCON, the South Tyrol Free Software Conference, is one of Europe’s most established annual conferences on Free Software. SFSCON promotes the use of Free Software in digital infrastructures as a tool to achieve greater innovation and competitiveness. Here decision-makers and developersmeet, learn and get inspired.

The exhibition will be hosted in the Crane Hall during SFSCON, on 13–14 November 2026. Afterwards, it will move to the coworking space NOISE, where it will remain on display until 19 December 2026. Both spaces are located on the ground floor of NOI Techpark’s main building.

Location
NOI Techpark
A. Volta Street 13A
39100 Bolzano, Italy

The exhibition is accessible during the regular opening hours of NOI Techpark:
Monday–Friday: 07:45–21:30
Saturday: 09:00–19:45
Sunday: Closed

title: The Exhibition at the Cybermois – Carrefour numérique in Paris – Oct. 3 to 31 2026
content:
The Code Source exhibition will be installed at the Carrefour Numérique², at the Cité des Sciences in Paris, during the Cybermonth, starting October 3, 2026.

The Carrefour Numérique² is a collaborative space dedicated to digital technology and user experience, located in the heart of the Cité des Sciences in Paris.

CYBER MONTH 2026 – Cybersecurity Month #5
October 3 to October 31
Through a program blending the history of computing, science, and digital practices, the Digital Crossroads² invites you to go behind the screen. Discover the codes that protect our communications, the traces we leave online, the stories of those who shaped computing, and the communities working towards a freer, safer, and more ethical digital world. A program to understand, experiment with, and better master our digital world. More info (in French)

title: Join the feed – Critical Code Studies Working Group – from Jan. 26 to 30 2026
content:
A discussion thread is dedicated to the exhibition during the Critical Code Studies Working Group, starting Monday January 26. Whether you’re a scholar, a dev, or a digital activist, join the conversation on the ethics and art of code curation. 

CCSWG is the major online think tank for Critical Code Studies, a hub of dialogue and collaborative inquiry that generates major thrust in the reading of code. Discussion and code critiques from previous working groups have appeared in electronic book review and have contributed to conference panels, essays, books, and more, including multiple book projects with The MIT Press and special issues of Digital Humanities Quarterly.

From Monday January 26 to Friday, 30 January 

Online at https://wg.criticalcodestudies.com/

title: Exhibition launch at UNESCO – The Software Heritage Symposium – Jan. 28 2026
content:
On January 28th, the annual Software Heritage Symposium, organized at UNESCO – Paris, will mark the 10th anniversary of the Software Heritage initiative. This event recognizes software source code as a universal component of the knowledge commons and organize collective action for its long-term preservation and inclusive reuse. 

On this occasion, the source code exhibition will be launched at UNESCO, offering hundreds of participants an exclusive preview.

The Symposium can also be followed online by registering on the event page. 

Interview of Roberto Di Cosmo by Delphine Sabattier – Politiques Numériques (POL/N).

About the exhbition from 00:14:14 to 00:15:00.
